question.en: In EF Core, which CLI command creates a new migration from your model changes?

options: dotnet ef database update
dotnet ef migrations add Init
dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold
dotnet ef database drop --force

explanation.en: `migrations add` diffs the model against the last snapshot and writes a migration class; `database update` is what applies it.

question.en: What does AsNoTracking() change in this EF Core query?

options: It skips the database cache
It loads every related entity
It runs the query as raw SQL
It skips change tracking

explanation.en: Entities are not added to the change tracker, which saves memory and time for read-only data; edits to them are not saved by SaveChanges.

explanation.en: One query loads the blogs, then touching each blog's Posts lazily fires one more query per blog: the classic N+1 problem.

question.en: What does Include do in this EF Core query?

options: Eager-loads each blog's posts
Keeps only blogs with posts
Lazy-loads posts on first use
Adds Posts as a new column

explanation.en: Include tells EF Core to load the related Posts with the blogs in the same round trip, avoiding a query per blog.

question.en: Which query is safe from SQL injection?

options: Only b, as Raw escapes quotes
Both, EF Core escapes input
Only a, {name} is a parameter
Neither, both paste raw text

explanation.en: FromSql takes a FormattableString and turns each interpolated value into a DbParameter; FromSqlRaw with string concatenation sends the input as SQL text.

question.en: On a relational provider, what happens to order1 when order2's insert fails?

options: It is rolled back as well
It stays saved in the table
It is retried on the next call
It is saved once order2 is fixed
answer: It is rolled back as well

explanation.en: By default SaveChanges wraps all its commands in one transaction, so if any statement fails none of the changes are committed.

question.en: How does Dapper supply the value for @age?

options: It pastes 30 into the SQL text
It reads a column named age
It binds it as a DB parameter
It asks SQL for a variable
answer: It binds it as a DB parameter

explanation.en: Dapper maps the anonymous object's properties to parameters by name, so @age is sent as a parameter, never spliced into the SQL.

question.en: Why do many SQL Server guides warn against AddWithValue here?

options: It sends the value as unescaped SQL
It infers NVARCHAR, hurting index use
It only works with stored procedures
It opens a second connection per call
answer: It infers NVARCHAR, hurting index use

explanation.en: A .NET string becomes NVARCHAR, so SQL Server converts the VARCHAR column to compare, which can turn an index seek into a scan. Set SqlDbType.VarChar explicitly.
